title: Deep-dive #3 of 4 — Candidate A: PROP-Graph Archaeology. Walk all ~127 PROPs, build a dependency graph, identify OBE-but-not-marked / wrongly-marked-implemented / broken-chain proposals. CLEAN the PROP-102/108 auto-close trust graph BEFORE enforce-mode flip. Fold high-signal doc-drift findings (PROP-116 Candidate E) into this deliverable as discovered.
context:
Per PROP-116 ranked_top_3[2]. Tinker's framing: 'Time-sensitive forward-value: cleans the PROP-102/108 auto-close trust graph BEFORE enforce-mode flip (prevents silent bad closures during the active period) and trims the 127-PROP per-run walk cost. Execution risk: Low-moderate; large corpus but mechanically walkable.'

The critical-path framing: PROP-102 + PROP-108 are currently in shadow mode (Phase 0). When operator flips them to enforce mode (PROP-102-enforce.flag, directive-auto-close-enforce.flag), the auto-close mechanisms will close PROPs and directives based on the verification_pattern / lifecycle linkage they read from the corpus. If the corpus contains:
  - PROPs wrongly marked 'implemented' that aren't (residue=0 fails — e.g. PROP-103 partially-implemented annotation already exists)
  - PROPs with stale supersedes_props / superseded_by_props pointers
  - OBE PROPs that should be closed but are still 'proposed'
  - PROPs whose verification_pattern script doesn't exist or doesn't grade A
Then enforce-mode would either silent-close bad ones (bad), refuse to close legit ones (annoying), or pollute the trust graph (worse, hard to detect).

This deep-dive cleans the corpus BEFORE the flip, removing the silent-bad-closure risk.

Fold-in: PROP-116 Candidate E (documentation hygiene pass) is folded into A. While walking PROPs, tinker will inevitably notice doc-drift between PROP text and current pipeline state (CLAUDE.md, prompt files). Capture high-signal doc-drift findings (not every typo) in the same deliverable.
task: Execute Candidate A per PROP-116 + the Candidate E doc-drift fold-in. Produce: (1) a PROP-graph audit report identifying ~10-20 candidates for cleanup (each with category: OBE-not-marked / wrongly-implemented / broken-dependency / stale-supersession-pointer); (2) for each candidate, a recommended action (close with metadata / annotate / mark superseded / leave); (3) propose-only PROP authoring for any non-mechanical cleanup that needs operator judgment; (4) high-signal doc-drift findings (CLAUDE.md or prompts/*.md sections that don't match current state) — concise list, not every typo.
deliverable_acceptance_criteria: PROP-graph audit report exists with per-PROP categorization (~10-20 entries). Each entry cites the specific field/value mismatch.
Recommended actions are concrete and operator-actionable (e.g., 'mark PROP-XXX status: obe with closure_reason'; not 'investigate PROP-XXX').
Doc-drift section is a concise list (~5-15 entries), each citing a specific file + line + the drift kind (cadence stale / PROP reference outdated / agent name renamed / etc.).
If tinker finds NO meaningful corpus issues (best case — corpus is clean), the report explicitly says so. Don't manufacture findings.
Auto-close-enforce-mode readiness statement: does the corpus pass the bar to flip PROP-102 + PROP-108 to enforce? Yes/no with evidence.
constraints: Propose-only on any new PROP authoring.
Standalone deep-dive — do not also process directive 005.
Doc-drift findings stay in this deliverable; do not author a separate PROP for doc-only fixes.

If the audit surfaces a load-bearing PROP that needs immediate operator attention (e.g., a verification_pattern would falsely close a PROP), surface it with HIGH severity in the report rather than burying it.
If the corpus is too clean to find ~10-20 candidates, report that. Don't pad the list.
